# Laravel Error: Array to String Conversion

When building a multi-role selection system in Laravel, developers often encounter the `Symfony\Component\VarExporter\Exception\ExceptionClass` or, more commonly, a PHP error message stating **"Array to string conversion."** This happens when your controller attempts to assign a collection of values to a property that expects a scalar integer. The root cause is almost always a mismatch between how data is submitted via a multi-select form and how the database column is defined.

In the scenario described, you are using Select2 with an HTML `<select>` element configured as `multiple='multiple'`. Your Blade template correctly iterates through roles:

```html
<select id="role" name="role_id[]" multiple='multiple' class="form-control js-example-basic-multiple">
    @foreach($roles as $role)
        <option value="{{$role->id}}">{{$role->name}}</option>
    @endforeach
</select>
```

The critical detail here is the attribute `name="role_id[]"`. This signals to PHP that the incoming request parameter will be an **array**. When you select multiple options, the browser sends something like `role_id[]=1&role_id[]=5&role_id[]=12`. Laravel's Eloquent query builder automatically converts this into a collection or array accessible via `$request->role_id`.

However, your database migration defines the `role_id` column as an `unsignedInteger`:

```php
$table->unsignedInteger('role_id')->default(1);
```

In your `store` method, you are attempting to save this data directly:

```php
$user->role_id = $request->role_id; // This is where the crash happens
$user->save();
```

This line triggers the error because `$user->role_id` expects an integer (or null), but `$request->role_id` is an array. PHP throws a fatal error when trying to cast that array into a string or integer context for assignment. Additionally, your validation rule `'role_id' => 'required|integer'` fails because the validator sees an array where it expects a single integer value.

### The Solution: Pivot Tables and Relationships

The architectural fix depends entirely on your data model. If `users` needs to hold a single role (a one-to-one relationship), you cannot use a multi-select form. You must restrict the UI to allow only one choice, or pick one from the array in the controller.

However, if the intention is for a user to belong to multiple roles simultaneously, your current schema is fundamentally incompatible with that requirement. An `unsignedInteger` column can only store one value. To support multiple roles per user, you must implement a **Pivot Table**.

You need to create a new migration to define the pivot table:

```bash
php artisan make:migration create_user_roles_table
```

In this migration, you would define the relationship between users and roles, typically storing IDs for both in two separate columns (`user_id` and `role_id`) with foreign key constraints. This structure allows a single user record to be linked to multiple role records without violating the integer constraint on any single column.

### Handling Single vs. Multiple Selections

If you are strictly building a one-to-one relationship (User has exactly one Role), but users expect to pick multiple options from the dropdown, you face a UX/schema conflict. You have two paths:

1.  **Force Single Selection:** Change your HTML to remove `multiple='multiple'` and ensure the user can only pick one role.
2.  **Process the Array in Controller:** If you must accept the array but only save one value (e.g., the first selected), you must sanitize the input before saving:

```php
$roleIds = $request->role_id; // e.g., [1, 5]
$primaryRoleId = reset($roleIds); // Get the first ID
$user->role_id = $primaryRoleId;
```

This approach wastes the data from subsequent selections but avoids the crash. It is generally better to align your schema with your business logic: use a pivot table for many-to-many relationships and a single integer column for one-to-one relationships.

### Validation Considerations

Finally, update your validation rules to match the data type you are actually handling. If you intend to handle arrays temporarily before processing them, change the rule to `'required|array'` or `'nullable|array'`. If you are switching to a pivot table, you will typically validate that at least one role ID exists in the array and perhaps limit the maximum number of selections allowed.
